city.caveat: This is the official city record as kept, without adjustments. It joins several observing sites over the years, and a move, a new instrument or the city growing around a station can shift readings (city growth mostly warms nights); NOAA's adjusted climate datasets correct for these. Treat any single number as approximate.

text.p_yest: The high of 43°F was typical for November 13. The normal high for the date is 48°F, and the record is 69°F (1989, 1999). The low of 31°F was typical for November 13.
text.t_rec: Milwaukee has nearly stopped setting record lows
text.p_rec: If Milwaukee's climate weren't changing, every year would have the same chance of holding a daily record. Since 2000, Milwaukee has set 6 standing record lows, far fewer than the 63 that chance alone would give, and 87 record highs, more than the 63 that chance alone would give. The 1930s hold the most record highs of any decade (55). Milwaukee's all-time high is 105°F, on July 24, 1934.
text.t_chg: Milwaukee has warmed, days and nights alike
text.p_chg: Across 155 complete years: Milwaukee's average low has risen +0.17°F per decade (95% range +0.10 to +0.24), about +2.7°F since 1871. Milwaukee's average high has risen +0.28°F per decade (95% range +0.22 to +0.34), about +4.3°F since 1871.
text.t_mon: Lows rose in 9 of 12 months. Highs rose in 11 of 12 months.
text.p_rain: Milwaukee's yearly precipitation has risen +0.32 inches per decade (95% range +0.12 to +0.52), about +4.9 inches since 1871. The 1991–2020 normal is 34.5 inches a year. The wettest year was 1876 (50.36 in); the driest, 1901 (18.69 in).
